subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Should OpenClaw prioritize compatibility-preserving incremental schema reduction or first define a general deferred tool-schema protocol for core and plugin tools?
rationale: Both approaches reduce overhead, but deferred loading changes provider and plugin contracts while channel-aware pruning must preserve cron, isolated-agent, and cross-channel behavior.

options.title: Incremental reduction first
options.body: Deduplicate prompt text, skip empty payloads, shorten descriptions, and add capability-aware pruning before designing deferred registration.

options.title: Deferred protocol first
options.body: Define a general name-and-description catalog with on-demand schemas for core and plugin tools before further local pruning.

options.title: Opt-in slim mode
options.body: Add an explicit operator setting that preserves existing defaults while allowing narrower schemas, accepting another configuration surface.

recommendation.title: Incremental reduction first
recommendation.body: Deduplicate prompt text, skip empty payloads, shorten descriptions, and add capability-aware pruning before designing deferred registration.
